question.problem: If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with mean $\mu =12$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=16,$ determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $0.1.$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Since the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{16}=4,$ we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{4}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.1.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sqrt{n}} & <0.1 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{4}{0.1} \\ \sqrt{n} & >40 \\ n & >{40}^{2} \\ n & >1\,600.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=1\,601.$
